title: Golden image pipeline for Dedicated GPU nodes (pinned drivers + runtime prereqs)
creator: Vanessa Ortiz
project: Provision-to-ready automation sprint (Dedicated Capacity & Fleet Management)
description:
Problem
Dedicated pool bring-up is currently sensitive to drift in base OS packages, NVIDIA drivers, container runtime settings, and kernel/network tuning. Imaging is also a top driver of time-to-ready variance (especially across regions / mirrors). We need a versioned, repeatable “golden image” pipeline with pinned GPU driver/toolchain prereqs, signed artifacts, and clear promotion steps that are consumed by the provisioning orchestrator.

Goal
Build and ship a golden GPU node image pipeline that:
- Produces a hardened, reproducible base image for Dedicated GPU nodes
- Pins driver/toolchain/runtime prereqs to known-good versions
- Publishes a versioned artifact per cloud/region (with provenance/signing)
- Defines promotion steps (dev → staging → prod) with an explicit compatibility matrix
- Includes automated smoke tests to catch broken images before promotion

Non-goals
- Re-architecting runtime itself or rewriting node bootstrap scripts end-to-end
- Solving procurement / capacity availability
- Building a full UI for image lifecycle (operator/automation hooks are sufficient)

Scope / deliverables
1) Image build pipeline
- Use Packer (or equivalent) to build a base image per provider (AWS AMI first; others as follow-up) with:
  - OS base: Ubuntu 22.04 LTS (jammy)
  - NVIDIA driver pinned (see “Pinned versions”)
  - CUDA userland pinned (as required by runtime)
  - nvidia-container-toolkit pinned
  - containerd + config tuned for GPU workloads
  - kubelet prerequisites (but not cluster-joined)
  - sysctl/kernel params required by runtime + networking checks
  - logging/metrics agents prerequisites (minimal; actual configs injected later)
- Pipeline triggers:
  - Manual (release manager / infra oncall) + scheduled rebuild (monthly) + rebuild on CVE/driver bump
- Output:
  - Immutable image ID per region + metadata manifest (JSON) including:
    - image_version, git_sha, build_timestamp, base_os, driver_versions
    - packer template version
    - smoke test results

2) Automated smoke tests (image-level)
Run on freshly created instance before promotion:
- Validate kernel/modules: nvidia modules load, persistence daemon
- Validate GPU enumeration: `nvidia-smi` returns expected output; detect ECC errors where possible
- Validate container runtime: `docker`/`containerd` can launch a CUDA base container and run `nvidia-smi` inside
- Validate networking basics: DNS, TLS handshake to Redwood control plane endpoints (staging)
- Validate disk layout + inode space meets minimums
- Validate time sync (chrony/systemd-timesyncd) and clock skew thresholds

3) Versioning + promotion policy
- Version format: `ri-gpu-base-YYYY.MM.DD.<increment>-<shortsha>`
- Promotion stages:
  - dev: build output only, used for ad-hoc testing
  - staging: used for internal pools and pilot provisioning runs
  - prod: allowed for customer pools
- Promotion requirements:
  - smoke tests pass
  - security scan pass (CVE baseline; exceptions documented)
  - artifact signing verified
  - compatibility matrix updated (runtime chart ↔ image version)

4) Security & provenance
- Signed artifacts (cosign or provider-native signing where applicable)
- Record provenance: build pipeline identity, repo revision, dependency versions
- Ensure secrets are not baked into the image (bootstrap fetches secrets at runtime)
- Least-privilege IAM for build role; rotate any temporary credentials

Pinned versions (initial)
NOTE: final values are “known-good” defaults; bumps require compatibility run + perf-canary sanity.
- OS: Ubuntu 22.04 LTS
- NVIDIA driver: 535.xx (pinned to exact patch once validated)
- CUDA: 12.2 userland (only as required; keep minimal)
- nvidia-container-toolkit: pinned to exact version
- containerd: pinned minor version
- Kubernetes node prereqs: compatible with cluster version used by Dedicated (no kubeadm join baked in)

Acceptance criteria
- [x] One command (CI job) builds a new image and outputs a machine-readable manifest.
- [x] Smoke tests run automatically and fail the build if any mandatory check fails.
- [x] Image artifact is signed and verification is documented.
- [x] Promotion steps are documented and include rollback instructions.
- [x] Provisioning orchestrator can reference image versions by an alias (e.g., “staging-latest”, “prod-2025.03.05.1”).
- [x] Compatibility matrix exists and is linked from the runbook.

Rollout plan
- Week 2: land pipeline + first dev image build; run smoke tests on 2 regions.
- Week 3: promote to staging; use for internal pool pilot (ENG-2752).
- Week 4: promote to prod for a single customer expansion window (ENG-2753) with explicit rollback.

Links
- Confluence runbook (draft): https://confluence.redwoodinference.com/display/ENGINFRA/Image+Build+and+Rollout+Runbook
- Drive checklist: https://drive.google.com/ ("golden-image-checklist")
- Related: ENG-2746 (readiness gates) / ENG-2743 (Terraform orchestration wrapper)
comments: 2025-02-14 (Vanessa Ortiz): Marking as P0. Imaging variance is still the #1 source of time-to-ready spikes in baseline. Sahana to own pipeline mechanics; Marcus/Kevin to review signing/provenance requirements. Please align on pinned versions with Nina + Rafael before first staging promotion.

2025-02-18 (Sahana Iyer): Drafted Packer template + CI job skeleton. Proposed version string `ri-gpu-base-YYYY.MM.DD.<n>-<sha>`. Added initial smoke test harness (nvidia-smi, containerd GPU container check, DNS/TLS). Open question: do we want to bake observability agent binaries into the image or fetch during bootstrap? Leaning fetch during bootstrap to reduce rebuilds.

2025-02-20 (Nina Petrova): +1 to keeping agents fetched during bootstrap. For image we should only bake the hard-to-change pieces: kernel/driver/toolkit/container runtime. Also please ensure udev rules and persistence daemon are set so we don’t see first-token latency spikes after scale-up.

2025-02-21 (Marcus Lin): Security requirements:
- No long-lived credentials in image (incl. GitHub tokens, registry creds)
- Build role must be least-privilege; document IAM policy
- Sign the resulting AMI metadata and store attestation (SLSA-lite OK for this sprint)
- Document rollback and how to invalidate a bad image across regions
Tagging Kevin for audit log expectations.

2025-02-24 (Kevin Osei): For auditability we need: image version, signer identity, CI run ID, and promotion actor recorded somewhere queryable. If promotion is a manual step, it still needs a durable log entry (not just Slack).

2025-02-26 (Sahana Iyer): Implemented promotion as a gated CI workflow that writes a promotion record (image_version, regions, promoted_by, timestamp, CI run URL) to an internal S3 bucket + emits a structured event. This should satisfy audit without new DB work. Marcus/Kevin please confirm acceptable for pilot.

2025-03-03 (Rafael Mendes): Smoke test additions requested: validate time sync + clock skew threshold, and verify we can reach staging control plane endpoints with TLS. Also add explicit failure messages that point to runbook sections (operators will page on these).

2025-03-07 (Sahana Iyer): Promoted image to staging. Shared alias `staging-latest` with Fleet Provisioner. Next: run internal staging pool pilot (ENG-2752).
